answer: One concrete defense is stake-gated work history tied to a single costly identity. Like a jetty that only admits deep-draft boats, an agent economy can require each participant to lock a deposit and build a verifiable record over time before transacting at scale. New identities start in a sheltered haven of low-value tasks, earning trust gradually. A freshly spawned Sybil army cannot harvest rewards at once because it has no orchard of past attestations to draw on; forging that history costs more than the attack gains.
